title: Critical Minimax Power under the Weak Null with Armwise Caps on Outcome-Dependent Missingness
banked_reason: D0.5 tier=subfield < floor=field, paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4, salvageable=false; independent main validity confirms no bounded same-topic field repair. Math and citations pass; informal result only, no Lean/F-stage certification.
gap_reasons: The delivered characterization covers balanced binary trials with unitwise outcome-mediated reporting and public potential-arm missingness caps; realized response rates do not establish those caps, and no delivered application validates them. The unrestricted original-record converse matches the exactly valid finite attainer in the critical limit, with no load-bearing conjecture or stale matched-frontier claim. Above the powerless phase, finite minimax power remains uncharacterized, and exact calibration relies on exhaustive enumeration. The matching planning-error order is a supremum over signal windows, with its lower bound forced by ceiling discretization already at m=0; it supplies neither an optimal approximation constant nor a fixed-signal lower rate. The certificate built from C_B=10^6 is trivial at realistic trial sizes, and the small-design computations do not establish the operational accuracy needed for the advertised planning use. Scalar historical priority remains unresolved, so contribution credit rests on the causal experiment and transfer arguments, with classical substrates attributed to [West (1987)](https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~mw/MWextrapubs/West1987a.pdf) and [Chen–Fang (2015), Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.3159); these scope and practical limitations constrain the projected score. proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the exact powerless boundary, finite exactly weak-null-valid nonoracle test, full-original-record converse, arbitrary-cap-sequence unknown-scale critical frontier, and a computable root-K planning envelope with interval-window lattice witnesses. The final math review passes and all five classical sources are attested, but the projected subfield tier (7.1) is below the field floor (7.4), with no bounded repair in scope. No F-stage or Lean artifact exists: this is an informal derivation, not a Lean-certified theorem; a duplicate planning theorem remains disclosed as editorial ballast.
tldr: Public armwise caps on potential missing outcomes determine worst-case causal power in a balanced binary trial with fixed potential outcomes, offsetting benefits and harms, and unitwise outcome-mediated reporting. Original-record indistinguishability gives \(P^\star=\alpha\) through \(s\le\min\{2m,n\}\). At \(s=2m+\lceil h\sqrt{n-2m}\rceil\), the full-record minimax power and a nonoracle, finite, exactly weak-null-valid rational rule converge to the explicit unknown-scale Gaussian value \(V_\alpha(h)=F_\alpha(h)\), uniformly on compact positive signal windows. The finite-to-critical bridge has a cap-uniform computable \(O(K^{-1/2})\) error envelope. Windows with nonempty interior also have legal fixed-table \(\Omega(K^{-1/2})\) lattice witnesses and a liminf lower constant equal to half the supremum of the branch derivatives over their interior. Thus the planning-error order is proved; exact or optimal leading constants and matching lower orders on empty-interior compact windows remain open.
gap: Heng--Zhang--Feng explicitly leave discrete-outcome weak-null inference as a research direction. Wu--Ding provide complete-data asymptotic weak-null validity, and Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix provide complete-data finite coordinatewise-bounded-null validity. Missingness completion and always-reporter results address other restrictions or populations; these guarantees do not characterize capped whole-trial aggregate weak-null minimax power.
fill: The main result pairs a full-record converse with a finite nonoracle rule at \(s=2m+\lceil h\sqrt{n-2m}\rceil\), and certifies the scalar value. The open question prices the finite-trial error for prospective planning.
